role: Standalone native LIVEFACTS_PROBE payload that answers loader-fact questions in its own process

artifact.format: ELF64 LE ET_DYN AMD64 (x86_64-sie-ps5), entry _start from SDK crt1.o, NOT a PRX

claims: The probe is a genuine SDK payload ELF built with the pinned prospero-clang wrapper, caller-local pinned linker script (link_layout.py sha-verified), crt1.o _start entry, --no-undefined, ET_DYN validated with exactly one PT_DYNAMIC and terminal DT_NULL.

Every dynamic import of the artifact is declared by pinned SDK target libs (12 imports; sce*/sysctl/getpid/open/write/close/__error from libkernel{,_web,_sys}.so, memset/memcpy/strlen from libSceLibcInternal.so/libc_stub_weak.so); table in receipt import_providers.
E7 needs no dynamic import: kernel_get_fw_version is DEFINED by crt1.o and statically linked (llvm-nm T evidence in receipt).
dlopen/dlclose resolve statically from libc.a(dlfcn.o) into crt1.o's bundled rtld __dlopen/__dlclose (link.map evidence); E6 retention goes through the SDK payload's own loader.
Worker-1 supplier TUs compile clean read-only with the same wrappers; recompiled object sha256 values are byte-identical to worker-1's receipt (bc7c6a43..., 76733b65...), proving reproducibility.
The record writer is host-tested with the pinned LLVM clang: escaping, 2KB bound, auto-comma JSON validity, truncation marking; all emitted demo lines parse with python json.loads.

The payload writes exactly one JSONL record per experiment (E1..E7 + summary) to /data/modbridge-livefacts-probe.jsonl, appends with O_CREAT|O_APPEND, exit 0/90/92 contract, no other /data writes, single main thread, no network, no console contact by build or worker.
honest_boundaries: Host evidence is compile/link/nm/objdump/disassembly only; NOTHING was executed on a PS5 target by this worker.
All E1..E7 runtime outcomes are unknown until the controller dispatches the artifact; the probe records actual rc/errno/values and never fabricates success.

E4's sceKernelGetModuleList has no SDK header; both the pinned prosperodev 3-arg spelling and the brief's 4-arg spelling are probed with both size units; the disassembly shows indirect calls with owned-scratch argument registers, but register-level safety on target is unverified until run.
E1 dereferences DT_DEBUG-derived pointers by design (that is the experiment); a corrupt r_map could fault the payload before later experiments — this risk is inherent to the question asked.
This worker never modified any file outside outputs/2026-10-04-zcode-team/worker-liveprobe/ and never reset/stashed/checked out anything in the Codex worktree.
